case-overload.title: Case 1: the TV next door
case-overload.prompt: Diagnose the interference, then choose the fix.

config.title: Case file: Mrs. Tremblay's television
config.story: Your neighbour's TV picture and sound break up whenever you transmit.
evidence: It happens on 80, 40, 20 and 15 m alike.
You added a low-pass filter at your transmitter. No change.
Your transmitter's harmonics measure well within limits.
config.caption: The TV sound breaks into a rough hiss each time you key the transmitter, whatever band you're on.

hints: Interference on every band points away from harmonics.
case-overload.success: Every band, clean transmitter: the TV is overloaded. A high-pass filter at the TV keeps your HF signal out.

case-desense.title: Case 2: Field Day

config.title: Case file: Field Day, 20 m
config.story: The 20 m SSB operator loses every signal whenever the 20 m CW station, 15 m away, transmits.
evidence: The CW station's signal isn't on the SSB station's frequency.
Weak signals vanish; strong ones just get quieter.
It stops the moment the CW station stops.
config.caption: A station comes through clearly, then fades almost to nothing while the CW station transmits, and returns when it stops.

case-desense.success: The strong nearby transmitter desensitizes the receiver. More distance between the stations and band-pass filters help.

case-intermod.title: Case 3: the jumbled frequency

config.title: Case file: the handheld on the roof antenna
config.story: You connected your VHF handheld to a high-gain outdoor antenna. Now your quiet simplex frequency is full of noise.
evidence: You hear several different signals at once, with different kinds of modulation.
There's a paging transmitter and a commercial base station nearby.
On the handheld's own small antenna, the frequency is clear.
config.caption: Two or three different voices and tones jumbled together on a frequency that should be empty.

case-intermod.success: Strong nearby signals mix in the receiver: intermodulation. A suitable filter at the receiver keeps them out.
